prereg.origin: the state curriculum worked (forward .107 -> .480, slip 6.31 -> 2.14 in the assist-then-release protocol) but the policy it produced carries nothing: support .388, non-foot 67.8 W, COM .583, and it even runs the body down into the floor. Support itself has never been a constraint in a distribution where it is violated.

change.state bank v2: recorded from two release rollouts (the state-curriculum model and the fast 1 ms model) so the bank contains both low-support and low-height states; per-state support and COM are saved with the bank so the coverage is auditable
change.three constraints: support (windowed minimum, target 0.90), non-foot contact (windowed maximum, target 4.889 W), COM height (windowed minimum, target 1.20), each with its own multiplier, dual ascent 0.05 per rollout on the mean violation, lambda_max 50
change.kept: 1 ms policy tick, base target 200 Hz, C = 0.02, 50 percent cold start plus 50 percent bank start, derived pad body R=.02, mu=1.5, releasable adhesion .25 body weight, reward v4, 42-joint PPO, 48 updates, gates unchanged

prereg.what_would_count_as_progress: support minimum at or above 0.90 with non-foot under 4.889 W in the assist-then-release protocol, while slip stays below 3; anything else is another recorded negative
prereg.labelling: derived channel plus replacement ANN; bank states are our own simulated history; not frozen-body acceptance and not connectome activity
prereg.accounting: all three multipliers and their violating statistics logged per update; bank composition (support and COM ranges) recorded in JSON; both evaluation protocols reported

adhesion.label: derived-channel: results are NOT frozen-body acceptance

state_curriculum.note: initial states recorded from our own simulation during the release phase; no external generator

action_joints: 1 ms tick, C=.02, state-curriculum v2, Lagrangian on support + non-foot + height
